sentence_stem: Not only did the team lose the match,
correct_completion: but they also lost their captain to injury.
full_sentence: Not only did the team lose the match, but they also lost their captain to injury.
acceptable_variants: but their captain was also ruled out with an injury.
but they also suffered a serious injury to their captain.

options.text: so they celebrated late into the night.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a result, but celebrating does not follow from the 'not only ... but also' structure, which needs a second negative outcome.

options.text: but they also lost their captain to injury.
and the match was held in the stadium.
options.why_wrong: This adds a neutral detail but does not complete the 'not only ... but also' pair, which needs a second negative outcome.
'Although' introduces a contrast, not the additive second item required by 'not only ... but also'.

grammar_focus: Correlative conjunctions 'not only ... but also' with subject-auxiliary inversion after 'not only'
explanation: After 'Not only did', the auxiliary moves before the subject, and the sentence needs an additive second clause introduced by 'but also', so the two outcomes are presented as cumulative. Speakers whose first language uses flexible word order may be tempted to skip this inversion, so it is worth practising as a fixed pattern.
translation: Yalnızca maçı kaybetmekle kalmadılar, kaptanlarını da sakatlık nedeniyle kaybettiler.
